whatFailed: POST /v2/bookings/{bookingUid}/reassign answered 200 with the envelope the docs require (status: success, data present) and the exact body its own DTO declares, {bookingUid, reassignedTo:{id,name,email,displayEmail}}, but the scenario asserted data.uid and data.hosts[0].id, two fields that no schema on either bound doc page defines.

observed: Step 1 created the round-robin booking (uid cVRx1La31YaHnjS7MPFz3F, host id 1 Reference Host). Step 2 POST /v2/bookings/cVRx1La31YaHnjS7MPFz3F/reassign with cal-api-version 2024-08-13 returned HTTP 200 in 31 ms with {"status":"success","data":{"bookingUid":"cVRx1La31YaHnjS7MPFz3F","reassignedTo":{"id":1,"name":"Reference Host","email":"reference-host@example.com","displayEmail":"reference-host@example.com"}}} (server.stdout.txt line 314). status matched the enum and data existed; only data.uid (and, had it been reached, data.hosts[0].id) was absent. The server mapped only the 2024-08-13 versions of both reassign routes (server.stdout.txt lines 174-175), and the only stderr noise is the sandbox mail server on port 1025 refusing connections, unrelated to the assertion.
impact: None for the asserted field: the response matched the product contract and the docs' only concrete promise (status + data). The real harm sits next to it: the published reassign response schema is self-referential, so no API consumer can learn the shape, and in Cal.diy the endpoint reports a successful reassignment it never performs.

rootCause.explanation: This is the root cause of the DOC defect that made the scenario guess, not of the failing assertion itself. The NestJS envelope class here is named ReassignBookingOutput_2024_08_13 and its data property is typed as the platform-types class of the SAME name (imported aliased at line 6, registered via @ApiExtraModels at line 8, $ref'd via getSchemaPath at line 15). Nest's Swagger plugin keys component schemas by class name, so the two collapse into one entry and the generated OpenAPI emits data.oneOf/allOf pointing back at the envelope itself: the published page therefore documents zero response fields. The prose at lines 16-17, carried verbatim into the docs, names ReassignAutoBookingOutput and ReassignManualBookingOutput, which exist nowhere in the codebase (only this string) and nowhere in the fetched doc corpus. The actual data shape is packages/platform/types/bookings/2024-08-13/outputs/booking.output.ts:415-426 (bookingUid + reassignedTo), materialized by getOutputReassignedBooking at apps/api/v2/src/platform/bookings/2024-08-13/services/output.service.ts:539-553, and that is exactly what the product returned. There is no uid or hosts anywhere on this response path, in this build or in the documented 2026-02-25 operation, whose declared response schema on the doc page is still ReassignBookingOutput_2024_08_13.

notes: Answering the round-robin edition question directly: the endpoint DOES exist in the tested tree. Both routes are declared in apps/api/v2/src/platform/bookings/2024-08-13/controllers/bookings.controller.ts:415-437 and 439-456 and were mapped at boot (server.stdout.txt lines 174-175), teams and round-robin event types still exist in the data model (the seed's 'Reference Team Round Robin' event type booked fine in step 1), and only the ENGINE was removed: packages/platform/libraries/index.ts:123-150 replaces roundRobinReassignment and roundRobinManualReassignment with empty async no-ops under the comment 'Round-robin reassignment removed (EE feature)'. bookings.service.ts:993-1048 awaits the no-op, re-reads the booking, and hands the unchanged host to getOutputReassignedBooking, which is why the response says reassignedTo id 1, the original host, in 31 ms with no calendar or email work. So Cal.diy answers 200 'success' for a reassignment that provably did not happen. That is a genuine edition-mismatch defect against the doc sentence 'Currently only supports reassigning host for round robin bookings', and it is worth filing on its own (a removed feature should 501 or 404, not report success), but it is NOT what step 2 asserted: the step only checked the envelope and the invented fields, and the scenario's own note already anticipated the no-op as product finding P7. Recommended scenario fix: assert data.bookingUid and data.reassignedTo.id (the real, code-declared contract) instead of data.uid and data.hosts[0].id, and add an assertion that reassignedTo.id differs from the original host if the intent is to prove reassignment actually moved the booking. Recommended docs fix for cal.com: rename one of the two ReassignBookingOutput_2024_08_13 classes (or pass an explicit @ApiExtraModels name) so the generated OpenAPI stops $ref-ing the envelope from its own data property, and delete the stale ReassignAutoBookingOutput / ReassignManualBookingOutput wording. Version-header note: this step deliberately sent cal-api-version 2024-08-13, a version Cal.diy actually serves, so systemic cause 1 (the missing 2026-02-25 version) is not in play here; step 3, the step that does send 2026-02-25, never ran because step 2 aborted the scenario, and the same is true of the six later steps including both named-route shape checks.
